title: UI/UX & Digital Experiences
intro: Make digital journeys easier to understand, navigate and use across the moments that matter.
audience: For product owners and marketing teams improving a website, interface or digital service where clearer journeys can help people complete their goals.
audiencePoints: Teams refining an existing product experience
Businesses planning a new service or interface
deliverables: Map audience needs, key tasks and points of friction in the current experience.
Organise navigation and content so people can find the next useful step.
Create responsive screens and interaction states for the agreed flows.
Supply annotated layouts and component guidance for implementation.
process: Review users, tasks and the current journey.
Prioritise flows, content and information architecture.
Prototype interface options and refine with feedback.
Document responsive states and handoff details.
faqs: What is included in a UX review?
The review focuses on the agreed tasks, pages and available source materials. Any user research or analytics work is scoped with the client.
Do you also develop the interface?
UI/UX design can be delivered on its own or alongside website development, depending on the project.
Can you improve one part of a digital product?
Yes. A project can focus on a particular flow, feature or set of screens when that is the clearest next step.
